nodes.label: Implicit state machine
nodes.rationale: A status enum alone does not capture guards and transitions; the audit groups related workflows into 44 families.

nodes.label: Unreleased stock holds
nodes.rationale: The audit found no release or expiry operation for held reservations, risking indefinite reduction of available stock.

nodes.label: Notification claim versus delivery outcome
nodes.rationale: Claiming an email before sending can leave a failed notification without a retry path.

nodes.label: Auth hydration identity race
nodes.rationale: A profile response for a previous identity could overwrite current client profile state.

nodes.label: Delivery confirmation record granularity
nodes.rationale: Legacy orders use an order timestamp; marketplace items use item timestamps, with product-level refund eligibility based on the earliest non-null item confirmation.

nodes.label: Time-driven eligibility state
nodes.rationale: Return, settlement and signed URL eligibility change as time passes even without a database write or UI event.

nodes.label: Coupled checkout, fulfilment and settlement workflow
nodes.rationale: The diagram describes linked but parallel states; one giant status would erase useful distinctions.

nodes.label: Administrator verified delivery confirmation
nodes.rationale: The admin verifies receipt offline, records a note, and confirms all items on a paid order; repeat requests do not restart the deadline.

nodes.label: Thirty-minute stock reservation expiry
nodes.rationale: Timed release restores computed purchasable stock; late provider success enters payment review to avoid overselling.

nodes.label: Late payment review after reservation expiry
Tracked paid-order email deliveries
nodes.rationale: Durable outcomes and idempotent retries distinguish provider acceptance from recipient delivery.
